title: Semantic HTML document skeleton
when: The user wants a starting HTML file or boilerplate, or asks to fix the structure of a page so it uses semantic elements and landmarks.
prompt:
Goal: A valid, semantic HTML document that later files can build on: complete head, landmarks, one h1 and nothing missing.
Steps:
1. Open with <!doctype html> and <html lang>; make <meta charset="utf-8"> the first head child, then the viewport meta (width=device-width, initial-scale=1).
2. Add a specific <title> (page, then site), a meta description of 50 to 160 characters, style.css, and the script with type="module" or defer.
3. Body order: skip link to #main, <header> with a <nav> holding a <ul> of links, <main id="main">, optional <aside>, <footer>.
4. Inside main: one h1, then <section> blocks each opened by an h2; <article> only for content that stands alone (a post, a card).
5. Choose elements by meaning: <button> for actions, <a href> for navigation, <time datetime>, <address>, <figure> with <figcaption>, lists for groups.
Quality bar:
- Each landmark appears once: header, nav, main, footer.
- Heading levels never skip.
- No div where a semantic element exists.
Pitfalls:
- A div with a click handler instead of a button.
- One h1 per section.
- Charset meta after the title, which can garble accents.
Verify:
- [ ] First line is <!doctype html>.
- [ ] Head has charset, viewport, title and description.
- [ ] The skip link targets the main id.
- [ ] Every tag is closed and ids are unique.
Output: index.html with the full skeleton and real content, linking style.css and main.js.

examples.input: me dá um html base bem estruturado para começar meu site
examples.output: index.html with lang="pt-BR", charset, viewport, skip link, header with nav, main with h1 and sections, footer
